label: Christie's London 1974 Hera auction lot 348
summary: Nine-line Syriac bowl for Prwkzʿd son of Kwmy, sold at Christie’s in 1974 and now unlocated.

source.title: Relics of Syriac Magic: Another Syriac Bowl for Prwkzʿd br Kwmy and a Syriac Incantation Fragment in the British Museum
source.citation: Moriggi, Marco. “Relics of Syriac Magic: Another Syriac Bowl for Prwkzʿd br Kwmy and a Syriac Incantation Fragment in the British Museum.” Folia Orientalia 61 (2024): 193–202. https://doi.org/10.24425/for.2024.152391.

claims.value_text: Clockwise spiral from centre to rim
Protection of the client's house, threshold, sons, and daughters

texts.content: Invokes angels to kill demons and protect Prwkzʿd son of Kwmy, his household, and children.

events.details: Sold as lot 348 in the Antiquities ‘Hera’ auction; present whereabouts unknown.

label: British Museum BM 117877 Syriac bowl fragment
summary: Eleven-line Estrangela-script fragment, formerly classified as a divorce document and newly edited as part of a Syriac incantation bowl.

source.title: Relics of Syriac Magic: Another Syriac Bowl for Prwkzʿd br Kwmy and a Syriac Incantation Fragment in the British Museum
source.citation: Moriggi, Marco. “Relics of Syriac Magic: Another Syriac Bowl for Prwkzʿd br Kwmy and a Syriac Incantation Fragment in the British Museum.” Folia Orientalia 61 (2024): 193–202. https://doi.org/10.24425/for.2024.152391.

claims.value_text: Probably clockwise spiral from bottom to rim
Possibly from a Rawlinson or Rassam Mesopotamian collection; exact origin uncertain

texts.content: Very fragmentary spell probably related to a dialogue between a magician and a demonic egg.

label: Davidovitz popularity-and-success bowl
summary: Jewish Babylonian Aramaic bowl published as a new charm for popularity and success in the Davidovitz Collection.

source.title: ‘My Foes Loved Me’: A New Incantation Bowl for Popularity and Success
source.citation: Ford, James Nathan. “‘My Foes Loved Me’: A New Incantation Bowl for Popularity and Success.” Mehqarim be-Lashon 20 (2023): 215–230 (Hebrew).

appearance.locator: pp. 215–230; newly published Davidovitz Collection bowl

texts.content: A favor charm intended to obtain popularity and economic success for its client.
